- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is falling.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is bullish; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 7 days if sentiment > 0.5.  
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5–7 days if sentiment drops below 0.0.
